risks.note: Management identifies this as one of the most critical threats given NSDL's role as India's largest depository and custodian of sensitive investor data. The risk covers potential unauthorised access, use, disclosure, disruption, modification or destruction of information and information systems; any breach could undermine trust in the financial system and invite severe regulatory and reputational consequences. Mitigated through ISO 27001:2022 certification, multi-layer controls using AI, next-generation firewalls, intrusion prevention systems, encryption at rest and in motion, privileged identity and access management, and a 24/7 in-house Security Operations Centre.
risks.risk: Information security and cyber security risk

risks.note: Listed by management as the impact of market behaviour on the Company's revenues and sustainability across business cycles. Management explicitly acknowledges a need to reduce reliance on equity-driven revenues, and flags that global inflation and geopolitical conflicts such as oil shocks and war-driven instability may reduce IPO activity and long-term retail participation, impacting NSDL's transaction-driven revenues.
risks.risk: Business risk — revenue sensitivity to market cycles and equity concentration

risks.note: Potential inability to conduct business and provide services due to damage to physical assets or infrastructure breakdowns caused by natural calamities, accidents or technical failures. As critical financial market infrastructure, an outage is systemic. Addressed by a BCP/DR policy compliant with SEBI circulars, an established Disaster Recovery Site from which depository operations are periodically conducted, regular mock and real-scenario drills, and a Near DR site acting as a data bunker for critical applications.

Compliance with the various laws and regulations governing the Company. As a Market Infrastructure Institution, SEBI and other regulators push for faster settlement cycles, stricter investor protection norms and enhanced transparency; management states these requirements increase costs, operational complexity and reputational risks if not managed effectively. All director appointments require prior SEBI approval, constraining board composition flexibility.
risks.risk: Legal, statutory and regulatory compliance risk

risks.note: Management notes that while NSDL is a dominant player, competition could impact its market share and revenue streams. It states it must increasingly onboard new-age fintech brokers to ensure it maintains a significant market share of the depository service market in India, and is educating brokers on mitigating the concentration risk of opening accounts with only one depository.

Risks associated with the increased use of technology in business operations. NSDL's entire franchise runs on proprietary platforms (SPEED-e, IDeAS, eDPM, the Digital Gateway APIs), and the industry transition to T+0 settlement will demand systems capable of handling real-time transactions, raising the cost and execution burden of platform modernisation.

Possible losses from operations due to third-party liability, employee infidelity, electronic and computer crimes, errors and omissions. Depository operations are executed through a closed user group of 311 Depository Participants and Registrars & Transfer Agents, so operational failures at intermediaries also transmit to NSDL.

Financial risks that can affect the ability of the Company to perform its functions. NSDL is additionally required under the SEBI (Depositories and Participants) Regulations, 2018 to set aside five percent of profits from depository operations to the Investor Protection Fund.

currentContext.expansion: NSDL is an asset-light market infrastructure institution and its expansion is platform, network and capacity build-out rather than physical plant. During FY 2025-26 the Company invested in platform modernisation, capacity, automation, cyber security and customer experience, capitalising approximately ₹106.1 Crore of technology investments including capital work-in-progress, and implemented 56 APIs (the NSDL Digital Gateway, spanning Account Management, Transactions and Reporting) to let Depository Participants, brokers, issuers and other intermediaries connect more efficiently with its systems. Network expansion added 21 Depository Participants during the year, taking the total to 311, providing services from over 57,037 service centres and branches in more than 2,060 cities and towns in India. New platform build-outs included automation of Value-Free Transfers of Government Securities through API integration with RBI's eKuber platform, CCIL and depositories; a Unified Digital Portal for Foreign Portfolio Investors and Foreign Venture Capital Investors offering single-window registration, compliance and onboarding; a digital facility for submission of Form 121 declarations under Section 393(6) of the Income-tax Act, 2025; and enhancement of SPEED-e to allow password-based users to submit off-market transfer instructions online with OTP-based authentication. Resilience capacity was extended through a Disaster Recovery Site, periodic operation of depository functions from that site, and a Near DR site implemented as a data bunker for critical applications. Geographic expansion is via GIFT City IFSC, where NSDL joined the MII consortium that formed India International Bullion Holding IFSC Limited, holding a 20% stake, and provided the securities depository software system to India International Depository IFSC Limited, enabling issuance of Unsecured Depository Receipts for NASDAQ and NYSE-listed companies traded on the NSE IFSC platform. Looking forward, management states it will intensify investment in advanced digital infrastructure, widen API offerings via an API sandbox mechanism, strengthen cybersecurity frameworks, and build systems capable of handling real-time transactions for the transition to T+0 settlement cycles.

- Potential inability to conduct business and provide services due to damage to physical assets or infrastructure breakdowns caused by natural calamities, accidents or technical failures. As critical financial market infrastructure, an outage is systemic. Addressed by a BCP/DR policy compliant with SEBI circulars, an established Disaster Recovery Site from which depository operations are periodically conducted, regular mock and real-scenario drills, and a Near DR site acting as a data bunker for critical applications.
- Compliance with the various laws and regulations governing the Company. As a Market Infrastructure Institution, SEBI and other regulators push for faster settlement cycles, stricter investor protection norms and enhanced transparency; management states these requirements increase costs, operational complexity and reputational risks if not managed effectively. All director appointments require prior SEBI approval, constraining board composition flexibility.
- Management notes that while NSDL is a dominant player, competition could impact its market share and revenue streams. It states it must increasingly onboard new-age fintech brokers to ensure it maintains a significant market share of the depository service market in India, and is educating brokers on mitigating the concentration risk of opening accounts with only one depository.
- Risks associated with the increased use of technology in business operations. NSDL's entire franchise runs on proprietary platforms (SPEED-e, IDeAS, eDPM, the Digital Gateway APIs), and the industry transition to T+0 settlement will demand systems capable of handling real-time transactions, raising the cost and execution burden of platform modernisation.
- Possible losses from operations due to third-party liability, employee infidelity, electronic and computer crimes, errors and omissions. Depository operations are executed through a closed user group of 311 Depository Participants and Registrars & Transfer Agents, so operational failures at intermediaries also transmit to NSDL.
- Financial risks that can affect the ability of the Company to perform its functions. NSDL is additionally required under the SEBI (Depositories and Participants) Regulations, 2018 to set aside five percent of profits from depository operations to the Investor Protection Fund.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Technology-led transformation: build advanced digital infrastructure, widen API offerings via an API sandbox mechanism, and strengthen cybersecurity frameworks to safeguard investor data, with systems capable of handling the transition to T+0 settlement cycles.
- Retail investor empowerment: expand investor education programmes and simplify access procedures, with special emphasis on tier-2 and tier-3 cities, leveraging mobile platforms, vernacular content and partnerships with intermediaries.
- Diversification of services away from equity-driven revenues, broadening offerings across debt …

hero.oneLiner: NSDL is a SEBI-regulated Market Infrastructure Institution and India's first and largest depository, holding assets under custody of ₹477.29 Lakh Crore as of March 31, 2026.
